analysis: The only changed file in this batch is docs/developer/build.md. The change documents CI behavior: push runs now ask the Darkbloom Sandbox routing plane the same way same-repository PRs do (head lines 269-273), and a new 'CI Caching' section (head 296-378) describes cache restore on all runs. Saves happen only on pushes to master/dev (SAVE_CACHES), and .git is validated with git fsck before use. Checkouts use persist-credentials:false, so the saved .git/config holds no job token. Sparse checkout skips large evidence archives. No runtime provider code, App Attest, attestation, key custody or coordinator-protocol behavior is modified. This is documentation only, and none of the TB-002 or TB-011 trust boundaries or controls are altered. I looked at the threat model's provider-centric assets and threats and found none that this change invalidates. The claimed CI controls (limiting cache saves to protected branches, which avoids PR cache poisoning, and branch_not_admitted gating on the routing plane) live in ci.yml, provider-ci-build/action.yml and darkbloom-route.yml, which are outside the supplied evidence. I could not verify that those workflow files actually implement them. The CI-supply-chain surface (release builds use literal Blacksmith labels; the docs say release, signing and publication jobs are not routed) is not a modeled boundary here. A later pass that sees the workflow files should confirm that SAVE_CACHES gating and the unrouted release lanes match this documentation. The head text unit was truncated at line 490, so the tail of the Verify section is unseen, but the patch shows no changes there.
